summary: Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Georgetown, Loyola Chicago, and a PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After completing a PhD at Stanford (~1980–1984) under William R. Hutchison, he served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).
Thomas Athol Joyce was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Hertford College (~1897–1901). He subsequently worked at the British Museum from around 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Appalachian State University as Assistant Professor of Religion (attested 2009).

Thomas Blom Hansen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Aalborg University. He held posts at the University of Natal, Edinburgh (~2000–2003), Amsterdam (~2003–2010), Yale (~2006–2008), and became Professor of Anthropology at Stanford University in 2010.

Thomas Borchert works in Buddhist and religious studies. A former PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), he held an appointment as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Indologist and linguist Thomas Burrow studied at Cambridge and SOAS. He held posts at the British Museum (1937–1944) and SOAS (1938–1948) before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit and fellow at the University of Oxford from 1944 to 1976.

Thomas Christian Tychsen was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kiel University (~1777–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1783), he held a post at the University of Göttingen from around 1788 to 1834.

Thomas Cleary worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a PhD from Harvard University, and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, later holding a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Art historian Thomas E. Crow studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, directed the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at NYU in 2007.

Thomas E. Wood is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his BA and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. He held posts at California State University, Fresno, and SUNY New Paltz.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indology and history scholar educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Ethelbert Page was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Shrewsbury School and St John's College (~1869–1873), and later held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD under Robert A. F. Thurman, 2003), he held a post as Executive Editor at Columbia University (attested 2007).

Thomas Henry Huxley was educated at Great Ealing School, Charing Cross Hospital Medical School (~1842–1845), and University College London. He held a post at Imperial College London from around 1854 to 1885.

Thomas James Mazanec specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, and received his PhD from Princeton University under supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

Thomas Jülch is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies educated at Goethe University Frankfurt, Hull, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich (PhD ~2006–2011). He was a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.
Thomas Kintaert is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at the University of Vienna, attested in 2009 and serving as a Lecturer attested from 2022 to 2026.
Thomas M. Hunter is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Dean at the University of Virginia and held an affiliation at the University of British Columbia (attested 2011).
